# Critique — Pattern 13 (Environmental)

The slot allocation across the 255 slots was distributed as follows: Air Quality (~15%), Water Safety & Occupational Exposure (~25%), Built Environment & Climate (~25%), Noise, Travel, & Disasters (~25%), and self-monitoring fillers (~10%). Reaching exactly 255 questions felt moderately forced; the last 15–20 questions (positions 235–255) served as filler/general monitoring checks. Overlaps exist with the Respiratory and Demographics domains (e.g., central HVAC filtration, housing stability, wildfire exposure) because air pollution and housing location represent critical environmental threats to respiration and are determined by socioeconomic context. The V-flag was systematically set to `true` on questions where a "Yes" answer indicates a protective choice or environment (e.g., using HEPA filters, filtering water, living in walkable neighborhoods, daily sunlight) to align with a convention where a stored bit `1` reflects risk or toxic exposure. We paraphrased concepts from standard social needs screening tools to ensure accessibility. The weakest question is position 253 ("Do you log your environmental symptoms weekly...") as the term "environmental symptoms" is awkward and lacks clear clinical classification.
